subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a cron-scoped tool-policy config surface, make cron runs inherit subagent tool policy, or intentionally leave cron restrictions limited to per-job `payload.toolsAllow`?
rationale: This sets a public config and security-boundary contract for scheduled autonomous runs, and the safest default depends on maintainer intent for upgrades, delivery semantics, and policy precedence.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce an explicit cron tool-policy config with documented precedence over global, sandbox, subagent, and per-job policy layers, plus upgrade-safe defaults.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Reuse `tools.subagents.tools` for cron sessions, reducing config surface but coupling two distinct session classes and risking unexpected upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Leave system-wide cron restrictions out of core and require operators to set `payload.toolsAllow` per job, accepting the current security and delivery ergonomics gap.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce an explicit cron tool-policy config with documented precedence over global, sandbox, subagent, and per-job policy layers, plus upgrade-safe defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest local history points to recent subagent/tool-policy work and prior review context on this exact issue.
